summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, streaming and token/sec benchmarking. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for production ML inference. Action items: benchmark template, POC window, security docs, pricing estimate.
topics: dedicated vs hosted vs private VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Sasha (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: Hey, Priya Menon, Head of ML at Cumulus. We run realtime summarization and ranked searches for our A/B product.
[00:15] Ethan: Ethan Clarke, platform engineering, I'll own the infra side.
[00:19] Maya: Maya Li, CTO, joining for architecture and security ques.
[00:23] Sasha (AE): Great, I'm Sasha, AE for Redwood, and Diego, our SE is here.
[00:28] Diego (SE): Hi all, Diego Ramos, focus on latency and throughput — happy to dig into benchmarks.
[00:33] Sasha (AE): Outline — want to understand your targets (p95, concurrency), current infra, and whether hosted vs dedicated vs private makes sense.
[00:41] Priya: High level — we need p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and under 1s for longer chat-like flows (~512 tokens). Concurrency spikes up to ~120-150 requests/sec during peak for the recommender.
[00:56] Ethan: Our current stack is a mix — some models on managed endpoints (vendor A), others on a self-hosted Triton stack for lower cost; but ops burden is high.
[01:07] Diego (SE): Cool, are those 120-150 concurrent in-flight requests or qps? Also, do you stream tokens to the client?
[01:15] Priya: That's concurrency, in-flight. Some flows do streaming for progressive responses, yes — low-latency streaming is important for UX.
[01:22] Maya: Also data residency and KMS integration matter for certain customers.
[01:27] Sasha (AE): Thanks — so three big constraints: p95 targets, concurrency and streaming, plus security. Diego, want to walk through how we benchmark?
[01:35] Diego (SE): Sure. For hosted we usually run token/sec tests at varying concurrency and measure end-to-end p95 including network. For dedicated we provide expected throughput per GPU SKU and can run an on-prem or VPC benchmark for exact numbers. Typical configs: sequence lengths 64, 128, 512; batch sizes 1-8; measure both with and without KV cache warm.
[01:56] Ethan: When you say p95 includes network, are you measuring from client to Redwood endpoint or inside the cluster? We need both.
[02:03] Diego (SE): Good call. We capture both: client-to-edge p95 (realistic) and internal model infer p95. For hosted we can instrument at token level and show per-token latency breakdown in Console.
[02:13] Priya: What's realistic for p95 on a single A100-equivalent? We saw varying numbers with other vendors.
[02:19] Diego (SE): Rough rule of thumb: for a 70B dense model quantized, single GPU can do ~10-20 tokens/sec depending on kernels; p95 latency for 128 tokens can be 200–600ms depending on batching. But with batching and KV-caching for streaming/prefix reuse we often hit sub-300ms for short seqs. Those are approximate — we prefer to run a targeted benchmark.
[02:39] Maya: We're evaluating dedicated reserved capacity if it means consistent p95 during spikes — unpredictable latencies from shared endpoints are a problem.
[02:47] Sasha (AE): Right, Dedicated buys you predictable throughput and capacity isolation; we also offer autoscaling and burst options.
[02:54] Priya: For streaming specifically, we care about token emission latency — after initial token, each subsequent token should be under 40ms ideally. Can Redwood guarantee that with hosted?
[03:04] Diego (SE): We instrument token pipeline: decoding + kernel + network push. On dedicated under optimal kernels, inter-token latency can be ~15-30ms. Hosted depends on plan (shared vs reserved), but we can run streaming stress tests during POC and provide SLA targets for dedicated.
[03:17] Ethan: Interesting. What about concurrency with batching — won't batching increase p95? During spikes we can't afford large batching delays.
[03:25] Diego (SE): Exactly. Continuous batching helps — the runtime continuously merges small requests without waiting for a full batch. You tune target batch latency thresholds. For strict sub-300ms p95 we recommend low max batch wait (e.g., 5-12ms) and a reserved pool to avoid cold queueing.
[03:43] Priya: Do you have examples of token/sec per GPU for quantized Llama-like models? Our models are roughly 7-13B and some 70B variants.
[03:53] Diego (SE): For 7-13B in int8/4-bit quant, single GPU can hit 150-400 tokens/sec depending on sequence length and kernel optimizations. 70B models are lower per-GPU, more like 10-50 tokens/sec. Again, configuration matters (FP16 vs 4-bit, KV cache reuse).
[04:13] Maya: Our concern: if we go hosted for cost, will we see noisy neighbor slowdowns?
[04:18] Sasha (AE): For hosted we have multi-tenant pools optimized by model profile; for higher SLAs we recommend Dedicated. Also smart routing can fall back to compatible variants if capacity constrained.
[04:28] Ethan: What's the typical setup for the POC? We want to run real traffic replay for a day.
[04:33] Diego (SE): We usually provide a benchmark spreadsheet and a runbook: step1 upload model or point to open variant, step2 run traffic replay with controlled concurrency ramp, step3 capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec, step4 test streaming and KV cache warm/cold. We'll include synthetic spike tests.
[04:50] Priya: Cool. For our SLOs we need p95 under 300ms for seq<=128 at concurrency 120, and steady token throughput to support 10k tokens/sec aggregate. Is that feasible?
[05:00] Diego (SE): Aggregate tokens/sec 10k is doable across a pool; with dedicated nodes we can model how many GPUs needed. We'll need your prompt distribution and average token lengths to estimate exact GPU counts.
[05:12] Priya: We'll share sample prompts and a traffic histogram.
[05:15] Maya: On security — VPC peering, private deployment, and KMS for key control are showstoppers for some customers. How does Redwood handle this?
[05:23] Sasha (AE): We support Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and SOC 2. We'll share the security pack.
[05:31] Ethan: For private, do you provide the control plane or is that self-hosted entirely?
[05:36] Diego (SE): Control plane can be customer-managed for private; we provide deployment artifacts and operators. For strict air-gapped we have on-prem packages. We can map out the network diagram in the next docs.
[05:46] Priya: Latency wise, private on-prem obviously removes network overhead but ops is heavy — cost tradeoff.
[05:52] Diego (SE): Exactly why some teams choose Dedicated in our cloud region closest to them — predictable latency with less ops burden.
[05:59] Sasha (AE): Quick interjection — any existing compliance requirements? HIPAA? PCI?
[06:03] Maya: A subset of customers are regulated; SOC2 is required and we prefer end-to-end encryption with KMS.
[06:09] Sasha (AE): We'll include SOC2 report and KMS integration notes with the security docs.
[06:14] Ethan: Back to benchmarks — can you show a sample report with breakdowns per-token, kernel time, queue time?
[06:20] Diego (SE): Yes, our Console shows token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. For POC we usually share the raw csv and a summarized report.
[06:29] Priya: How do you measure p95 for streaming — do you include time to first-byte?
[06:33] Diego (SE): We measure time-to-first-token (TTFT) and inter-token latency. For streaming UX TTFT under 200ms and inter-token under 50ms is a common target.
[06:43] Priya: Also what about warm vs cold KV cache effects?
[06:46] Diego (SE): Cold KV cache can add significant latency on longer seqs; we run both cold and warm scenarios. For flows with heavy prefix reuse, caching reduces per-token compute drastically.
[06:57] Maya: On concurrency management — do you have backpressure controls and graceful degradation?
[07:02] Sasha (AE): Yes, we support rate limiting, per-route quotas, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to smaller models to maintain availability.
[07:10] Ethan: Pricing question real quick — how different is hosted vs dedicated on unit cost?
[07:15] Sasha (AE): Hosted is usage-based and easier to start; dedicated has a reserved monthly commit but lower unit costs at scale. We'll provide illustrative numbers in the pricing draft.
[07:25] Priya: For the POC we prefer Redwood to run hosted endpoints with a reserved pool so we can simulate dedicated-level isolation but with faster setup. Is that doable?
[07:33] Diego (SE): Yes, we can provision a reserved capacity slice in hosted environment for POC. That gives predictable performance for your test window.
[07:40] Maya: What telemetry will you provide during the POC? We need token-level metrics, tail latencies, and per-instance CPU/GPU utilization.
[07:47] Diego (SE): We'll provide Console access with dashboards and raw exports. We'll also include a tracing hook you can pipe to your APM.
[07:55] Sasha (AE): Let's talk schedule — proposed POC week Jan 25-29. Any conflicts?
[07:59] Priya: Works for us, we'll confirm by end of week.
[08:03] Ethan: We'll need the benchmark template earlier to map traffic.
[08:06] Sasha (AE): We'll send it today.
[08:09] Priya: One last technical — for 70B variants, do you recommend model parallelism or sharded GPUs?
[08:15] Diego (SE): For 70B we typically run multi-GPU sharding or use optimized kernel packs; dedicated deployments allow you to size the cluster. We'll include suggested topologies in the runbook.
[08:25] Maya: Any gotchas around SSO/SAML or IAM for private deployments?
[08:29] Sasha (AE): We integrate with SSO/SAML and support fine-grained RBAC; details in security bundle.
[08:34] Priya: Great. If we meet the p95 targets in hosted reserved POC, we'll evaluate Dedicated for production.
[08:39] Sasha (AE): Sounds like a plan. Recap and next steps coming up — Diego?
[08:43] Diego (SE): Recap: we'll send benchmark template and runbook, provision reserved slice for POC week, run traffic replay, collect p50/p95/p99 and token/sec, test streaming and KV cache warm/cold, and share security docs & pricing.
[08:57] Priya: Thanks, that's clear.
[09:00] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[09:02] Sasha (AE): We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[09:06] Ethan: Thanks, bye.
[09:08] End of recording (approx 42 minutes).
